about: The rulers of Dia-thìr, age by age, with their births, accessions and deaths: every ruler, holder under the king, keeper of the flame, rìgh and ban-rìgh, crowned ruler, council head, Commissioner, maor, Moot speaker and high custodian of the Rite named in the master annals, books and appendices, and the unnamed generations and rulers the arithmetic needs. The source of truth for rulers' ages: the master record, the era plans (eras/age_*/PLAN_people.json) and the era books keep to it. Years are era years ("LE 92"); *_y are years of the continuous count; ages are whole years. accession null with in_office set: the rolls give only a year in office. died null: the record does not tell the death (reign_end is then the last year the ruler is known to rule). gen: generations after Ailean Mòr, for his kin. Written by the lead; checked by check_rodais.py and eras/check_era.py (eras/quality/ages_check.py).

rule.owner: State rulers' ages, and enforce ages returning to normal by the Holy Age.
rule.long_years: The power of the coals was Ailean Mòr's alone (4,626 years, slain). His children born after the grove had long years, and every generation after him has fewer: the longest life in a generation is never longer than the longest in the generation before, and no child of the kin outlives the span of its long-lived parent. The long years run out in the Holy Age: in the Line of Aisling with Ceallach (FE 79), in the ruling line of Ìomhar and Goraidh with the last of the eleven unremembered rulers (FE 1,190).
rule.ordinary: No one born in FE 1,200 or later lives past 95: not in the Holy Age after its long years, nor in the Age of Sundering, the Age of Strangers, the Age of the Kingdom or the Age of Dubhan. Those born before the grove and those not of the king's blood never had the long years. The one exception the owner made is the coal-blooded (fuil-ghuail) of the Age of Strangers on, who bond with the vein and do not age; they are not rulers, and the check leaves them out by name.
